<description>
This implements the following actions from #35904:

1. **Expose the validation interface**

   Make the existing `CheckBlockHeader`, `ContextualCheckBlockHeader`, and `ContextualCheckBlock` functions part of the public validation interface by declaring them in `validation.h`.

2. **Interface Segregation: Remove dependency on `ChainstateManager`**

   `ContextualCheck*` functions need a  `ChainstateManager` only to access the
  consensus parameters. Pass `Consensus::Params` instead and access them at the call site.

3. **Make environmental dependencies explicit**

   Pass the validation time explicitly to `ContextualCheckBlockHeader` instead of reading the system clock internally.
</description>

[2026-10-22] rc:4347194712 inline on src/test/validation_check_header_tests.cpp by purpleKarrot (member) (edited 2026-10-22):
I am not sure we use the same definition of the word "declarative". I think the test cases that @janb84 contributed are very close to a declarative ideal: They are independent and each test case is responsible for the setup of its test data. Some procedural code remains, which is due to how the types under test are implemented.

To explain, code like the following implements a state machine:

```cpp
CBlockHeader header;
header.nVersion = ...;
header.hashPrevBlock = ...;
...
```

The variable `header` starts its life in the default state, with every new assignment to its data members being a state-transition for the value of the whole. The following would be a declarative alternative, where no later state transition of the test data is even possible:

```cpp
const auto header = CBlockHeader{
  .nVersion = ...,
  .hashPrevBlock = ...,
  ...
};
```

However, as long as `CBlockHeader` prevents aggregate initialization by providing a default constructor, some procedural code has to remain. Adding/removing/modifying constructors for primitive types is outside the scope of this PR.

But I assume this is not what you meant here. Please clarify.
